name: Isometric Illustration
visualIdentity: A projection method, not a full style definition: objects align to consistent isometric axes with clear scale, depth, and occlusion. Use parallel lines, limited colors, light shadows, and readable flat 2D labels. An overhead game view alone is insufficient.
suitableUses: Explicitly: isometric scenes, 3D dioramas, miniature sets, and layered, paper craft, collage, or 2.5D artwork. Inferred: useful for spatial overviews, infrastructure, logistics, systems, and processes when objects and relationships explain the subject.
limitations: Avoid camera tilt, perspective shrinkage, broken ground contact, exposed layer gaps, excessive depth, or obscured labels. Use motion-017 only for separable components whose relationships an exploded reveal explains; never explode decoration. The style is supplemental, not a claimed source-collection style.
palette: Use task, brand, or approved reference colors first; otherwise optional suggestions are background #F3EFE5, foreground #2D444D, sage #6E9990, and terracotta #C98961. Keep four discrete tokens, with no gradient; preserve semantic roles and asset colors. Sage and terracotta are decorative fills, not body-text backgrounds for the suggested foreground. Recheck contrast in the composite.
motionAndInteraction: Move, assemble, and separate objects along established axes without perspective shrinkage. Use an orthographic camera at isometric orientation or consistent SVG geometry. Motion candidates are optional: constrained depth parallax; chapter handoffs; story steps; or component reveals when supported. Video uses deterministic composition time; interactive HTML may map pointer, focus/tap, or scroll to bounded progress, with reversible states and reduced-motion access.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Synchronize with motion and narration, then check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Provide or create geometry or consistent isometric artwork, plus separable layers when animating depth or components. Labels should remain 2D and readable. Load fonts and assets; cache stateful simulations and seed randomness. Example terrarium elements are optional, not requirements.
combinations: Alone suits self-explanatory spatial scenes. With style-097, add verified data labels and comparisons in flat 2D; do not invent values or distort comparisons with extruded charts. With style-109, draw connectors only along isometric axes, with consistent stroke and no tangled routes. Skip near-duplicate Isometric Motion Graphics.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion engine by visual fidelity and action; Three.js with OrthographicCamera supports true 3D, while SVG can draw planar geometry without a 3D engine. Assign one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the composition, timing, sync, validation, and export default; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, recording the reason. Neither defines the visual style. Interactive input is not a video driver.
